correctness.rationale: The cyclic incidence map identifies the vertex-phase quotient with the edge torus because the only compatibility condition for integrating the differences is closure. The real stationarity equations have common flux s; strict descent in the claimed interval excludes additional modular fixed points. At s=0 the even number of pi entries gives eight points. At nonzero s the three unit-weight angles each equal a or pi−a; the two mixed branch counts require (t−1)sin a=0, while the two pure branch counts are the same set under a↔pi−a. The triple-angle identity then gives sin² a=(3t+1)/(4t), impossible below 1 and giving exactly four distinct solutions above 1. For the Boolean two-pi points, let d_i=−w_i cos z_i. The constrained Hessian determinant in coordinates u4=−u1−u2−u3 is (product d_i)(sum 1/d_i)=sign(d1)(1−t), and the two sign pairs yield both signs of the form. Translation by pi on all four coordinates reverses the Hessian, pairing the six non-extremal Boolean points by index. For a non-Boolean point the form is c[(2t+1)u1²−u2²−u3²−u4²], c=cos a≠0: its sign on u1=0 is opposite its sign on (−3,1,1,1). This gives the stated indices and a unique minimum. Reflection exchanging the endpoint pair of the special edge and the opposite pair gives Laplacian blocks [[1,−1],[−1,1]] and [[2t+1,−1],[−1,3]], yielding the stated spectral bound. The vertex potential's Hessian is bounded in operator norm by that Laplacian norm, giving the descent inequality by Taylor integration; summability gives vanishing gradients and increments. A finite omega-limit set with vanishing increments is a singleton. The nonminimum local null-basin argument also works at a zero stable multiplier: in a small coordinate ball the derivative splits into stable norm <1 and unstable least expansion >1, with a sufficiently small Lipschitz nonlinear remainder. A difference in the unstable cone (unstable norm at least stable norm) stays in the cone and expands, so two orbits trapped in the ball cannot have a difference in that cone. The trapped set is a Lipschitz graph over a subset of stable coordinates and is null. The analytic Jacobian is nonzero at the all-zero point, hence has a null zero set, and countable local inverse charts off that set ensure null sets have null preimages. This proves almost-everywhere selection including noninvertible updates. At antiphase the multipliers are 1−h lambda; strict linear attraction holds exactly in the claimed interval for positive h. Neither t=1 nor nonlinear behavior at the upper step endpoint is asserted. Replay: RESULT.md lines 19–58 and the determinant, block and cone checks above. The finite NumPy checker and verification notes were read, not executed, and do not prove exhaustiveness.

originality.rationale: Prior work covers the unit-weight rings, the general descent and finite-critical-set convergence argument, generic complex root counts and a signed-edge 12-real-root example. The distinct claim is the exact positive one-edge detuning census and its indices, yielding a unique attracting minimum throughout the descent range even where global invertibility is not available. No inspected stronger theorem gives the full census or that weighted specialization.
residual_risks: Bounded discovery and targeted source reads cannot exclude an equivalent all-positive C4 detuning classification in the Kuramoto or active-power-flow literature. Closest actual prior theorems were credited rather than dismissed on terminology alone.
Claims are confined to the positive detuned regime and the specified step interval; the earlier unweighted and signed regimes are not presented as newly solved.
